cves.summary: vLLM versions before 0.28.0 fail to validate audio sample rate headers in the transcription endpoint, allowing authenticated clients to bypass duration checks. Attackers can submit forged FLAC headers with inflated sampl
cves.headline: vLLM before 0.28.0 lets a signed-in client crash the API with forged audio headers

name: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
title: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in model serving, where a service accepts compressed or encoded input and expands it without a size limit. The one CVE here is in vLLM, an LLM serving engine, before version 0.28.0. A signed-in client sends a request with forged audio headers, and the server tries to decode the audio, which expands into far more data than the request itself. That lets an attacker crash the API and take the serving process down for other users. The pattern is the same wherever AI products decode audio, images or archives on the request path, and the harm is denial of service rather than data theft.
description: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles a compressed input with a very high compression ratio that produces a large output.

consequences.note: System resources, CPU and memory, can be quickly consumed. This can lead to poor system performance or system crash.

extended_description: An example of data amplification is a decompression bomb, a small ZIP file that can produce a large amount of data when it is decompressed.
